title: Deuteronomy 31: Moses' Final Charge and the Rebellion Foretold
body:
Read the chapter → [Deuteronomy 31](/bible/deuteronomy/31)

## Introduction

This session covers [Deuteronomy 31](/bible/deuteronomy/31) through 34, the close of the Torah. These are some of the most monumental chapters for identifying who we are today: we have already been through [Genesis 49](/bible/genesis/49), [Deuteronomy 28](/bible/deuteronomy/28), and [Leviticus 26](/bible/leviticus/26), and today we cover [Deuteronomy 33](/bible/deuteronomy/33), the blessing that shows where the tribes of Israel are geographically in these last days. Moses, barred from the promised land, spends his final days giving the children of Israel prophecy: chapter 31 is his charge and the warning of rebellion to come, chapter 32 is the song of Moses, chapter 33 is the blessing of the tribes, and chapter 34 is his death in the mount.

**[Deuteronomy 31:1-2](/bible/deuteronomy/31#v1)**

> <sup>[1](/bible/deuteronomy/31#v1)</sup> And Moses went and spake these words unto all Israel.
>
> <sup>[2](/bible/deuteronomy/31#v2)</sup> And he said unto them, I am an hundred and twenty years old this day; I can no more go out and come in: also the Lord hath said unto me, Thou shalt not go over this Jordan.

- Moses is one hundred and twenty years old this day, and the Most High has told him he shall not go over this Jordan. After he was provoked by the people at the waters of strife, he did not sanctify the Most High before the children of Israel, so he was barred from entering the promised land.
- The Most High lets him go up on the mountain to take a look at the land, but he will not enter into it. Before his farewell, chapters 31 through 33 give the children of Israel prophecy of what would happen to them.

**[Deuteronomy 31:3-6](/bible/deuteronomy/31#v3)**

> <sup>[3](/bible/deuteronomy/31#v3)</sup> The Lord thy God, he will go over before thee, and he will destroy these nations from before thee, and thou shalt possess them: and Joshua, he shall go over before thee, as the Lord hath said.
>
> <sup>[4](/bible/deuteronomy/31#v4)</sup> And the Lord shall do unto them as he did to Sihon and to Og, kings of the Amorites, and unto the land of them, whom he destroyed.
>
> <sup>[5](/bible/deuteronomy/31#v5)</sup> And the Lord shall give them up before your face, that ye may do unto them according unto all the commandments which I have commanded you.
>
> <sup>[6](/bible/deuteronomy/31#v6)</sup> Be strong and of a good courage, fear not, nor be afraid of them: for the Lord thy God, he it is that doth go with thee; he will not fail thee, nor forsake thee.

- The Most High himself goes over before Israel to destroy these nations, and Joshua goes over before the people, as he did to Sihon and Og, kings of the Amorites.
- The nations are given up before Israel's face so that Israel may do to them according to all the commandments already given: when you enter the land, follow the guidelines of [Deuteronomy 7](/bible/deuteronomy/7). Do not take their daughters for wives or give your sons to theirs, do not worship their gods, but utterly burn their gods with fire.
- Be strong and of a good courage, fear not, for the Most High goes with thee; he will not fail thee, nor forsake thee.

  Precepts:
  - **[Deuteronomy 7:3-5](/bible/deuteronomy/7#v3)**
    > <sup>[3](/bible/deuteronomy/7#v3)</sup> Neither shalt thou make marriages with them; thy daughter thou shalt not give unto his son, nor his daughter shalt thou take unto thy son.
    >
    > <sup>[4](/bible/deuteronomy/7#v4)</sup> For they will turn away thy son from following me, that they may serve other gods: so will the anger of the Lord be kindled against you, and destroy thee suddenly.
    >
    > <sup>[5](/bible/deuteronomy/7#v5)</sup> But thus shall ye deal with them; ye shall destroy their altars, and break down their images, and cut down their groves, and burn their graven images with fire.

    Make no marriages with the nations of the land, but destroy their altars and burn their graven images with fire.

**[Deuteronomy 31:7-8](/bible/deuteronomy/31#v7)**

> <sup>[7](/bible/deuteronomy/31#v7)</sup> And Moses called unto Joshua, and said unto him in the sight of all Israel, Be strong and of a good courage: for thou must go with this people unto the land which the Lord hath sworn unto their fathers to give them; and thou shalt cause them to inherit it.
>
> <sup>[8](/bible/deuteronomy/31#v8)</sup> And the Lord, he it is that doth go before thee; he will be with thee, he will not fail thee, neither forsake thee: fear not, neither be dismayed.

- Moses calls Joshua in the sight of all Israel and charges him: be strong and of a good courage, for thou must go with this people into the land sworn to their fathers, and cause them to inherit it.
- The Most High goes before Joshua; he will be with him and will not fail him. Fear not, neither be dismayed.

**[Deuteronomy 31:9-13](/bible/deuteronomy/31#v9)**

> <sup>[9](/bible/deuteronomy/31#v9)</sup> And Moses wrote this law, and delivered it unto the priests the sons of Levi, which bare the ark of the covenant of the Lord, and unto all the elders of Israel.
>
> <sup>[10](/bible/deuteronomy/31#v10)</sup> And Moses commanded them, saying, At the end of every seven years, in the solemnity of the year of release, in the feast of tabernacles,
>
> <sup>[11](/bible/deuteronomy/31#v11)</sup> When all Israel is come to appear before the Lord thy God in the place which he shall choose, thou shalt read this law before all Israel in their hearing.
>
> <sup>[12](/bible/deuteronomy/31#v12)</sup> Gather the people together, men, and women, and children, and thy stranger that is within thy gates, that they may hear, and that they may learn, and fear the Lord your God, and observe to do all the words of this law:
>
> <sup>[13](/bible/deuteronomy/31#v13)</sup> And that their children, which have not known any thing, may hear, and learn to fear the Lord your God, as long as ye live in the land whither ye go over Jordan to possess it.

- Moses wrote this law and delivered it to the priests, the sons of Levi that bear the ark of the covenant, and to all the elders of Israel.
- At the end of every seven years, in the solemnity of the year of release, in the feast of tabernacles, the law was to be read before all Israel: gather the people together, men and women and children, that they may hear, learn, and fear the Most High, and observe to do all the words of this law. The law had to be taught over and over to remind the people what would befall them and what they must do.
- Their children which have not known any thing must hear and learn to fear the Most High. The first thing you establish with your children, before they know anything else, is who they are and who their God is.

  Precepts:
  - **[Zephaniah 2:1](/bible/zephaniah/2#v1)**
    > <sup>[1](/bible/zephaniah/2#v1)</sup> Gather yourselves together, yea, gather together, O nation not desired;

    Gather yourselves together, yea, gather together, O nation not desired.

**[Deuteronomy 31:14-18](/bible/deuteronomy/31#v14)**

> <sup>[14](/bible/deuteronomy/31#v14)</sup> And the Lord said unto Moses, Behold, thy days approach that thou must die: call Joshua, and present yourselves in the tabernacle of the congregation, that I may give him a charge. And Moses and Joshua went, and presented themselves in the tabernacle of the congregation.
>
> <sup>[15](/bible/deuteronomy/31#v15)</sup> And the Lord appeared in the tabernacle in a pillar of a cloud: and the pillar of the cloud stood over the door of the tabernacle.
>
> <sup>[16](/bible/deuteronomy/31#v16)</sup> And the Lord said unto Moses, Behold, thou shalt sleep with thy fathers; and this people will rise up, and go a whoring after the gods of the strangers of the land, whither they go to be among them, and will forsake me, and break my covenant which I have made with them.
>
> <sup>[17](/bible/deuteronomy/31#v17)</sup> Then my anger shall be kindled against them in that day, and I will forsake them, and I will hide my face from them, and they shall be devoured, and many evils and troubles shall befall them; so that they will say in that day, Are not these evils come upon us, because our God is not among us?
>
> <sup>[18](/bible/deuteronomy/31#v18)</sup> And I will surely hide my face in that day for all the evils which they shall have wrought, in that they are turned unto other gods.

- The Most High tells Moses his days approach that he must die, and to call Joshua to the tabernacle to receive his charge; the Most High appears in the pillar of a cloud over the door of the tabernacle.
- The Most High tells Moses straight out: after you sleep with thy fathers, this people will rise up and go a whoring after the gods of the strangers of the land. The people Moses spent forty years tending will forsake the covenant, and instead of utterly destroying the nations and their gods, they will mingle with the nations and serve their gods.
- Then his anger is kindled, he forsakes them and hides his face, and many evils and troubles befall them, the same evils we just read through in [Deuteronomy 28](/bible/deuteronomy/28).
- You wonder where the Most High was when our babies were used as alligator bait, when we were packed on ships, hung, burnt, and raped in front of our own. His face was hid, because when he would have dwelt among us we went a whoring after other gods, so he left us in the hands of the people that hate us.

  Precepts:
  - **[Deuteronomy 28:15](/bible/deuteronomy/28#v15)**
    > <sup>[15](/bible/deuteronomy/28#v15)</sup> But it shall come to pass, if thou wilt not hearken unto the voice of the Lord thy God, to observe to do all his commandments and his statutes which I command thee this day; that all these curses shall come upon thee, and overtake thee:

    If thou wilt not hearken to observe all his commandments, all these curses shall come upon thee.

**[Deuteronomy 31:19-21](/bible/deuteronomy/31#v19)**

> <sup>[19](/bible/deuteronomy/31#v19)</sup> Now therefore write ye this song for you, and teach it the children of Israel: put it in their mouths, that this song may be a witness for me against the children of Israel.
>
> <sup>[20](/bible/deuteronomy/31#v20)</sup> For when I shall have brought them into the land which I sware unto their fathers, that floweth with milk and honey; and they shall have eaten and filled themselves, and waxen fat; then will they turn unto other gods, and serve them, and provoke me, and break my covenant.
>
> <sup>[21](/bible/deuteronomy/31#v21)</sup> And it shall come to pass, when many evils and troubles are befallen them, that this song shall testify against them as a witness; for it shall not be forgotten out of the mouths of their seed: for I know their imagination which they go about, even now, before I have brought them into the land which I sware.

- Write ye this song and teach it the children of israel, put it in their mouths, that this song may be a witness against them. We read chapter 32 as verses, but it was really given as a song, because what is in the form of a song is easily remembered and retained.
- When they come into the land that floweth with milk and honey and have eaten and waxen fat, they will turn unto other gods and serve them; then this song shall testify against them as a witness, for it shall not be forgotten out of the mouths of their seed.
- The Most High says, I know their imagination which they go about, even now, before I have brought them into the land. He already knew how they would forsake him when they got there.

**[Deuteronomy 31:22-26](/bible/deuteronomy/31#v22)**

> <sup>[22](/bible/deuteronomy/31#v22)</sup> Moses therefore wrote this song the same day, and taught it the children of Israel.
>
> <sup>[23](/bible/deuteronomy/31#v23)</sup> And he gave Joshua the son of Nun a charge, and said, Be strong and of a good courage: for thou shalt bring the children of Israel into the land which I sware unto them: and I will be with thee.
>
> <sup>[24](/bible/deuteronomy/31#v24)</sup> And it came to pass, when Moses had made an end of writing the words of this law in a book, until they were finished,
>
> <sup>[25](/bible/deuteronomy/31#v25)</sup> That Moses commanded the Levites, which bare the ark of the covenant of the Lord, saying,
>
> <sup>[26](/bible/deuteronomy/31#v26)</sup> Take this book of the law, and put it in the side of the ark of the covenant of the Lord your God, that it may be there for a witness against thee.

- Moses wrote this song the same day and taught it the children of Israel, and gave Joshua the son of Nun his charge.
- When Moses made an end of writing the words of this law in a book, he commanded the Levites that bear the ark to put the book of the law in the side of the ark of the covenant, that it may be there for a witness against thee.

**[Deuteronomy 31:27](/bible/deuteronomy/31#v27)**

> <sup>[27](/bible/deuteronomy/31#v27)</sup> For I know thy rebellion, and thy stiff neck: behold, while I am yet alive with you this day, ye have been rebellious against the Lord; and how much more after my death?

- I know thy rebellion, and thy stiff neck. If anybody knew Israel's rebellion, Moses knew: a stiff neck means you are told what to do and you refuse to do it, and Israel kept that spirit even after judgments, miracles, and harsh consequences.
- All forty years in the wilderness Moses was grieved; every day there was some issue, some drama the children of Israel raised. We think we grieve dealing with a congregation of a few hundred; Moses dealt with the rebellious spirits of all twelve tribes, thousands upon thousands.
- Israel became a burden to Moses to the point he asked the Most High to kill him rather than let him see his own wretchedness. While I am yet alive with you this day, ye have been rebellious against the Lord; and how much more after my death?

  Precepts:
  - **[Exodus 32:9](/bible/exodus/32#v9)**
    > <sup>[9](/bible/exodus/32#v9)</sup> And the Lord said unto Moses, I have seen this people, and, behold, it is a stiffnecked people:

    The Most High himself said, I have seen this people, and, behold, it is a stiffnecked people.
  - **[Hebrews 3:16-17](/bible/hebrews/3#v16)**
    > <sup>[16](/bible/hebrews/3#v16)</sup> For some, when they had heard, did provoke: howbeit not all that came out of Egypt by Moses.
    >
    > <sup>[17](/bible/hebrews/3#v17)</sup> But with whom was he grieved forty years? was it not with them that had sinned, whose carcases fell in the wilderness?

    Some when they had heard did provoke, and he was grieved with them forty years in the wilderness.
  - **[Numbers 11:11-15](/bible/numbers/11#v11)**
    > <sup>[11](/bible/numbers/11#v11)</sup> And Moses said unto the Lord, Wherefore hast thou afflicted thy servant? and wherefore have I not found favour in thy sight, that thou layest the burden of all this people upon me?
    >
    > <sup>[12](/bible/numbers/11#v12)</sup> Have I conceived all this people? have I begotten them, that thou shouldest say unto me, Carry them in thy bosom, as a nursing father beareth the sucking child, unto the land which thou swarest unto their fathers?
    >
    > <sup>[13](/bible/numbers/11#v13)</sup> Whence should I have flesh to give unto all this people? for they weep unto me, saying, Give us flesh, that we may eat.
    >
    > <sup>[14](/bible/numbers/11#v14)</sup> I am not able to bear all this people alone, because it is too heavy for me.
    >
    > <sup>[15](/bible/numbers/11#v15)</sup> And if thou deal thus with me, kill me, I pray thee, out of hand, if I have found favour in thy sight; and let me not see my wretchedness.

    Moses' grief: wherefore hast thou afflicted thy servant, the burden of all this people is too heavy for me; kill me, I pray thee, and let me not see my wretchedness.

**[Deuteronomy 31:28-29](/bible/deuteronomy/31#v28)**

> <sup>[28](/bible/deuteronomy/31#v28)</sup> Gather unto me all the elders of your tribes, and your officers, that I may speak these words in their ears, and call heaven and earth to record against them.
>
> <sup>[29](/bible/deuteronomy/31#v29)</sup> For I know that after my death ye will utterly corrupt yourselves, and turn aside from the way which I have commanded you; and evil will befall you in the latter days; because ye will do evil in the sight of the Lord, to provoke him to anger through the work of your hands.

- Gather unto me all the elders of your tribes and your officers, that I may speak these words in their ears, and call heaven and earth to record against them.
- I know that after my death ye will utterly corrupt yourselves, and evil will befall you in the latter days. This is heavy: Moses says evil shall befall the people he is speaking to in the latter days, meaning the last days, because they would do evil in the sight of the Lord to provoke him through the work of their hands.
- How did Moses know what would happen to the rebellious Israelites in the latter days? The Most High did not only give Moses the ten commandments on Sinai; he told him many wondrous things and showed him the secrets of the times. That is how Moses wrote Genesis, and that is how he saw ahead of time our people going into captivity again by slave ships, as [Deuteronomy 28:68](/bible/deuteronomy/28#v68) declares. The prophecies of chapters 32 and 33 are still unfolding to this very day.

  Precepts:
  - **[2 Esdras 14:3-5](/bible/2-esdras/14#v3)**
    > <sup>[3](/bible/2-esdras/14#v3)</sup> Then said he unto me, In the bush I did manifestly reveal myself unto Moses, and talked with him, when my people served in Egypt:
    >
    > <sup>[4](/bible/2-esdras/14#v4)</sup> And I sent him and led my people out of Egypt, and brought him up to the mount of where I held him by me a long season,
    >
    > <sup>[5](/bible/2-esdras/14#v5)</sup> And told him many wondrous things, and shewed him the secrets of the times, and the end; and commanded him, saying,

    On Sinai the Most High told Moses many wondrous things and showed him the secrets of the times and the end.

**[Deuteronomy 31:30](/bible/deuteronomy/31#v30)**

> <sup>[30](/bible/deuteronomy/31#v30)</sup> And Moses spake in the ears of all the congregation of Israel the words of this song, until they were ended.

- Moses spake in the ears of all the congregation of Israel the words of this song, until they were ended. The song itself is chapter 32.
